events.title: EDF issues potential air threat alerts across southern, eastern Estonia

articles.text: News ERR News {{1794373860000 | amCalendar}} share Facebook X (Twitter) e-mail Alerts about a possible air threat were issued on November 11, 2026. Source: ERR News News The Estonian Defense Forces issued a series of potential air threat alert warnings early on Wednesday morning as Ukraine reportedly attacked Russia's Ust-Luga Port with drones. The warnings were lifted at around 5:30 a.m. At around 3:15 a.m., residents in southern Estonia – Tartu, Jõgeva, Viljandi, Valga, Võru and Põlva counties – were told there was a "potential air threat" and to "seek shelter if you spot a drone." This was extended to the eastern Lääne-Viru and Ida-Viru counties at around 3:30 a.m. The warnings were lifted at around 6:30 a.m. A spokesperson from the Estonian Defence Forces told ERR that NATO fighter jets were scrambled in response. A resident from Kohtla-Järve in Ida-Viru County told ERR they had heard several jets flying over the area at short intervals. Latvia and Lithuania also issued drone warnings on Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning. Air threat alerts were issued across Estonia on Wednesday 11, 2026. Source: Helen Wright/ERR Alerts about a possible air threat were issued on November 11, 2026. Source: ERR News Ukrainian drones struck the Ust-Luga Baltic Sea port in western Russia's Leningrad Oblast overnight, monitoring channels reported, the Kyiv Independent said . The Governor of Leningrad Oblast, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said a drone attack had caused a fire in the port area of Ust-Luga by the Baltic Sea, around 36 kilometers from Estonia, injuring three workers, Reuters news agency reported. Ust-Luga is a major oil, oil products and grain export outlet, along with other commodities. The facility has been sanctioned by the European Union, Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Switzerland for its role in Russia's war against Ukraine. The port is "used to transport Russian crude oil by using the shadow fleet and other irregular and high-risk shipping practices," according to the European Commission's Directorate-General for Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood. Several alerts have been issued this year in Estonia as Ukraine has increased its attacks on Russia's oil industry, including Ust-Luga. The most recent was issued in September. Drone parts and debris have previously been found in all three Baltic countries and Finland after Ukrainian attacks on Russian infrastructure. Trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. are taking place in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. Ust-Luga fire visible from Estonia On Wednesday morning, ERR's correspondent Dmitry Fedotkin in Ida-Viru County reported that the attack on the Russian Port of Ust-Luga could be seen from Narva, Sinimäe and Sillamäe. Photographs and video show orange flames flickering on the horizon across the Baltic Sea. Watch the video below. -- Follow ERR News on Facebook and Twitter and never miss an update! events.title: US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia

articles.text: Image: Getty via Unsplash+ US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia A 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, British authorities announced Tuesday. The unnamed soldier was arrested by U.K. counterterrorism police “working closely” with U.S. authorities, including the FBI and the military, the Metropolitan Police said in a statement. The man is in custody at a London police station. “While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message—this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners,” FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement issued by the British counter-terror police. The man was arrested under sections of the U.K.’s National Security Act that cover espionage. The arrest occurred near Gloucester, a city about 100 miles west of London that is close to the home of GCHQ, Britain’s intelligence, security and cybersecurity agency. “As part of the investigation officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire,” according to police. “The country to which the allegations relate is Russia.” Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the head U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, said in a statement that the “senior soldier” who was arrested was “entrusted with sensitive information.” Earlier this year, Britain’s spy chief warned that Russia is engaged in “daily hybrid activity” against the U.S. and its Western allies. GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler accused Moscow of “relentlessly targeting critical infrastructure, democratic processes, supply chains and public trust” and that it attacks “from the seabed to cyberspace.” The Kremlin did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Government News News Briefs No previous article No new articles Martin Matishak is the senior cybersecurity reporter for The Record. Prior to joining Recorded Future News in 2021, he spent more than five years at Politico, where he covered digital and national security developments across Capitol Hill, the Pentagon and the U.S. intelligence community. He previously was a reporter at The Hill, National Journal Group and Inside Washington Publishers.
